_comment: Single source of truth for real external competitor agents used for
MEASUREMENT ONLY (#78, ADR-0008 amendment 2026-08-18). These are never
vendored into this repo -- scripts/fetch_external_agents.py reads this
file and downloads each entry into a gitignored local directory
(external_agents/ by default). No third-party code is committed to git.
Every entry's license was checked by the #67 survey before being added
here; do not add an entry without a confirmed permissive license.

agents.name: pilkwang_structured_economic_policy
agents.attribution: pilkwang, "Kaggriculture: Structured Economic Policy" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/pilkwang/kaggriculture-structured-economic-policy), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: Kaggle notebook; the submittable agent lives in the single code cell tagged with the `%%agentfile` cell magic (writes kaggle's main.py). The fetch script extracts that cell only -- the rest of the notebook is narrative/plotting for the writeup and is not fetched or executed.

agents.name: madhur_sabherwal_hub_geometry_agent
agents.attribution: Madhur Sabherwal, kaggriculture-hub-geometry-agent (https://github.com/Madhur-Sabherwal/kaggriculture-hub-geometry-agent), MIT License.
agents.notes: Structurally distinct job-scoring approach (hub geometry), picked for strategic diversity per the #67 survey.

agents.name: seyamalam_candidate_v6_adaptive_livestock
agents.attribution: Seyamalam, Kaggriculture (https://github.com/Seyamalam/Kaggriculture), agents/candidate_v6_adaptive_livestock.py, MIT License.
agents.notes: DO NOT fetch this author's candidate_v7_public_v18/v19/v20/v21 -- those are 300KB+ compressed-blob replayers, explicitly rejected by the #67 survey. Only v1-v6 (plain heuristic agents) are in scope, and only v6 is vendored here.

agents.name: alexandergremyakov_harvest_pulse_goose_dividend_v2
agents.attribution: Alexander Gremyakov, "harvest-pulse-goose-dividend-v2" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/alexandergremyakov/harvest-pulse-goose-dividend-v2), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: Kaggle notebook; single code cell tagged `%%writefile /kaggle/working/main.py`. The fetch script extracts that cell only.

agents.name: premaananda108_ecobot_v7
agents.attribution: premaananda108, "Economics-Driven Rule Agent (EcoBot v7) + Arena" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/premaananda108/economics-driven-rule-agent-ecobot-v7-arena), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: Public 819.0 / best 995.2 -- the strongest agent in this pool, and well above our own ~520-535. Its notebook tags TWO cells: main.py (the agent) and arena.py (a self-play harness); cell_file pins the former, so do not remove it (#151). Measured share ~0.792 vs DEFAULT_ANCHORS. Roughly 2.5x slower per game than the other externals.

agents.name: shashankjangid_agent_v300_champion
agents.attribution: Shashank Jangid, kaggriculture-agent (https://github.com/ShashankJangid/kaggriculture-agent), agent_v300_champion.py, MIT License.
agents.notes: The near-parity rung: measured share ~0.536 vs DEFAULT_ANCHORS (0.5 is parity). Chosen with v1000 to span a real measured spread. That repo has 57 agent files whose version numbers do NOT track strength -- v25_master is the weakest measured (~0.095) and v9 beats v100_sota -- so do not add rungs by version number without measuring (#151).

agents.name: shashankjangid_agent_v1000_sovereign_prime
agents.attribution: Shashank Jangid, kaggriculture-agent (https://github.com/ShashankJangid/kaggriculture-agent), agent_v1000_sovereign_prime.py, MIT License.
agents.notes: The strong rung: measured share ~0.677 vs DEFAULT_ANCHORS, beating every one of our anchors. Do NOT also add agent_v1500_sovereign_apex -- it measures ~0.674, within the ~0.01 run-to-run noise, so it is a duplicate voice for double the runtime (#151).

agents.name: adilshamim8_kaggriculture_grandmaster_starter
agents.attribution: adilshamim8, "Kaggriculture: From First Sprout to Grandmaster" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/adilshamim8/kaggriculture-grandmaster-starter), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Kaggle notebook; single code cell tagged `%%writefile submission.py`, imports `math` only. Public/best 387.5.

agents.name: songoku2005_kaggriculture
agents.attribution: songoku2005, "Kaggriculture" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/songoku2005/kaggriculture), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Kaggle notebook; single code cell tagged `%%writefile submission.py`. Pulls CROPS/ANIMALS from `kaggle_environments.envs.kaggriculture.kaggriculture` itself rather than hardcoding them. Public 445.5 / best 450.1.

agents.name: chaimaamatrag_kaggriculture_competition
agents.attribution: chaimaamatrag, "Kaggriculture Competition" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/chaimaamatrag/kaggriculture-competition), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Kaggle notebook; the notebook never uses the `%%agentfile`/`%%writefile` cell-magic convention at all, so `cell_index` (#229) selects the plain `def agent(obs):` code cell directly by position -- the only viable extraction path for a notebook like this. Self-contained single cell, 7.2KB.

agents.name: dianatofficial_reactive_agent_strategy_eda
agents.attribution: dianatofficial, "Kaggriculture: Apex Algorithmic Strategy & Economic Simulation" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/dianatofficial/kaggriculture-reactive-agent-strategy-eda), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Kaggle notebook; no `%%agentfile`/`%%writefile` magic anywhere, so `cell_index` selects the agent-definition code cell directly. The submittable callable is named `apex_agent(obs)`, not `agent` -- `entrypoint: "apex_agent"` (#229) has the fetch script append `agent = apex_agent` so the file still resolves under harness.external_pool's fixed `agent` contract. Self-contained, 3.1KB.

agents.name: georgymamarin_visualized_what_every_crop_pays
agents.attribution: georgymamarin, "Kaggriculture, Visualized: A Beginner's Guide to Every Mechanic (and What Every Crop Pays)" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/georgymamarin/kaggriculture-visualized-what-every-crop-pays), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Kaggle notebook; single code cell tagged `%%writefile main.py`. "Carrot Crew" -- the survey's own naming for this agent -- is deliberately simple; vendored as a **floor anchor**, not a ceiling voice. 3.7KB.

agents.name: paiky1995_inside_the_market_machine
agents.attribution: paiky1995, "Inside the Kaggriculture Market Machine" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/paiky1995/inside-the-kaggriculture-market-machine), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Kaggle notebook is analysis-only (its own words: "This one contains no agent") and never uses `%%agentfile`/`%%writefile`, so `cell_index` selects the `make_farm_agent(sell_mode)` factory cell directly. `sell_mode` is a parameter, not a fixed agent -- `entrypoint: 'make_farm_agent("daily")'` (#229) picks the sell_mode the notebook's own comparison recommends: its playbook section 7 states "Unsold goods are worth $0 at turn 720; cash is the only score" and "hold-and-dump lost every episode to an identical farm", i.e. `daily` (cash out every turn) beat `enddump` (hold and dump at day 28) in the notebook's own head-to-head. Vendored as `daily`, not `enddump`.

agents.name: raykkretzschmar_rank_your_agent_floor_anchor
agents.attribution: raykkretzschmar, "Kaggriculture: rank your agent against a known ladder" (https://www.kaggle.com/code/raykkretzschmar/kaggriculture-rank-your-agent), Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). CAVEAT from the survey: the notebook's headline 2563.4/2990.4 score belongs to a 120KB `zlib`+`b64`-packed opponent ladder in a separate cell (opaque -- rejected, never fetched). `cell_file: "my_agent.py"` pins the OTHER tagged cell -- the tiny naive tutorial challenger this notebook actually teaches -- so do not read this agent's local measurement as anywhere near 2990; it is a **floor anchor only**, 1.5KB.

agents.name: loubaliber_kaggriculture_loubal
agents.attribution: loubaliber, kaggriculture-loubal (https://github.com/loubaliber/kaggriculture-loubal), submission.py, MIT License.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Self-described rolling-horizon MPC (model predictive control) -- architecturally unlike anything else in the pool, picked for strategic diversity. 39KB, module-level `def agent(obs):`.

agents.name: shashankjangid_agent_v9
agents.attribution: Shashank Jangid, kaggriculture-agent (https://github.com/ShashankJangid/kaggriculture-agent), agent_v9.py, MIT License.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). A third measured rung from this author, alongside the existing v300/v1000 entries -- the #151 note on this repo already records that v9 beats v100_sota despite the version numbers not tracking strength. stdlib (`math`, `collections`). Do not add further rungs from this repo's 57 agent files without measuring first (#151).

agents.name: driw0x_kaggriculture_chi7
agents.attribution: Driw0x, Kaggriculture (https://github.com/Driw0x/Kaggriculture), src/agents/chi7.py, Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Fixed tile-layout planner: a module-level `CROP_STATE` dict hardcodes a crop assignment per board coordinate. 24KB, module-level `def agent(obs):`.

agents.name: darunesh1_kaggriculture_baseline_v1
agents.attribution: Darunesh1, Kaggriculture (https://github.com/Darunesh1/Kaggriculture), baselines/v1/main.py, MIT License.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Explicitly a frozen, self-contained baseline per the repo's own naming. 10KB, module-level `def agent(obs, config=None):`.

agents.name: naisha123_kaggriculture_agent
agents.attribution: Naisha-123, Kaggriculture_Agent (https://github.com/Naisha-123/Kaggriculture_Agent), agent.py, Apache License 2.0.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). The survey listed this as plain stdlib, but did not catch that the file's actual submission entry point is a module-level `my_agent(obs)` wrapping a per-player-keyed factory -- there is no module-level `agent` at all (found only by reading the fetched file directly, not by the survey's smoke test description). `entrypoint: "my_agent"` (#229) has the fetch script append `agent = my_agent`. 8.9KB, stdlib.

agents.name: lonespear_kaggriculture_v21
agents.attribution: lonespear, kaggriculture (https://github.com/lonespear/kaggriculture), main_v21.py, MIT License.
agents.notes: 2026-09-06 re-survey (#229). Needs numpy + scipy (module-level `try: import numpy; from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment` for a Hungarian-algorithm worker assignment, with a graceful stdlib fallback if unavailable). Taken despite the dependency: harness/external_pool.py's own docstring is explicit that externals are "opponents and gate opponents only, never submission candidates" (scripts/submit.py never packages one, per ADR-0005), and ADR-0008's stdlib-only citations ("stdlib-only in the submitted artifact (ADR-0004)") are all scoped to what WE submit, not to measurement opponents. 47KB, module-level `def agent(obs):`.
